team.claim: Official leadership page lists Melanie Perkins as CEO/co-founder, Cameron Adams as CPO/co-founder and Zach Kitschke as CMO. Undated page snapshot as of 2026-10-21.
TechCrunch identifies Cliff Obrecht as co-founder and COO as of 2026-02-18.
Founder backgrounds: Perkins and Obrecht previously launched Fusion Books in 2007; Adams was formerly a lead designer at Google. Historical company announcement as of 2013-03-20.

Head of design Andrew Green announced his departure in April 2026 and said he would remain an adviser. He joined Canva in October 2018 after roles at SEEK; he cited parenting and personal projects as his next focus.

AFR reported growth lead Iain Dowling resigned after eight years and senior engineering director Jonathan Ross would leave at end-May 2026. Reported as of 2026-05-18; the opened excerpt does not establish final exit dates or involuntary termination.

funding.claim: Company announcement: US$200 million funding round at US$40 billion valuation, led by T. Rowe Price, with Franklin Templeton, Sequoia Capital Global Equities, Bessemer, Greenoaks, Dragoneer, Blackbird, Felicis and AirTree participating; as of 2021-09-15.

Reuters reported launch of an employee stock sale at a US$42 billion valuation on 2025-08-20. This is secondary employee liquidity, not evidence of US$42 billion raised or new operating capital. Transaction proceeds and final close were not verified.

Latest identified priced transaction remains the August 2025 US$42 billion employee sale, but Forbes Australia reported lower investor marks as of 2026-06-30: T. Rowe Price implied US$38.2 billion and Franklin Templeton US$39.3 billion; it also reported Blackbird at US$34.9 billion. These are holder valuations, not new financing rounds.

output.verdict: Canva appears to have substantial product adoption and an expanding enterprise business, supported by company-reported end-2025 ARR of US$4 billion and a continuing profitability claim. Before investing, reconcile reported revenue with audited accounts and scrutinize AI costs and growth revisions, investor valuation markdowns, reporting controls, leadership succession and IP/security exposure; the last employee-sale valuation should not be treated as an assured exit price.

business.claim: Canva sells an online visual-communication and collaboration platform spanning presentations, documents, whiteboards, video, websites, spreadsheets and AI-assisted content creation. Company claim; product description as of 2025-06-11.

Freemium subscription model: Free, paid Pro for individuals, per-person Business for individuals and teams, and sales-led Enterprise with security, provisioning and governance controls. Eligible schools and nonprofits receive premium features free. Product-page snapshot as of 2026-10-21; no single global price assumed.
Company claim: serves enterprises, small businesses, consumers and students in more than 190 countries. Undated company press-hub snapshot, as of 2026-10-21.
TechCrunch reports the majority of business comes from North America, with lower-priced subscriptions offered in markets including Pakistan, Uruguay, Morocco and Jamaica; as of 2026-02-18.

traction.claim: Company claim, reported by TechCrunch: more than 265 million monthly active users and 31 million paid users at end-2025; monthly active users increased 20% during 2025.

Company claim as of 2025-06-11: Canva is used by 95% of the Fortune 500; named Enterprise customers include FedEx, Salesforce, Expedia, Reddit, Docusign and Zoom. Usage penetration is not equivalent to company-wide paid Enterprise adoption.
Company claim as of 2025-06-11: Enterprise go-to-market partners include resellers SoftBank and CDW, agency Designit and consultancy Deloitte; integrations include LinkedIn and HubSpot.

Company claim as of 2026-10-05: 100 million teachers, students and administrators use Canva; email-less student accounts are being expanded worldwide. Education adoption should not be treated as paid subscriber growth.

red_flags.claim: Execution and valuation risk: reported AI-cost-related rollout delays and a reduced 2026 growth forecast accompany lower investor marks than the last employee-sale valuation. Verify the revised plan and AI unit economics before underwriting the prior price.

Governance diligence: paid infringement notices for late financial reporting warrant review of reporting controls, despite the subsequent timely FY2025 filing and absence of an admission of liability.
IP risk: the upheld interim India feature restriction warrants review of patent exposure, product workarounds and litigation reserves; it is not a final finding on damages.

Leadership continuity: the reported design, growth and engineering departures during 2026 warrant retention and succession diligence; the evidence does not establish involuntary exits or a common cause.

Security diligence should test remediation of the historical direct breach and third-party creator-data controls; the disclosed third-party exposure alone does not establish a new Canva-system compromise.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor aggregator snapshot as of 2026-10-21: 3.8/5 from 904 anonymous reviews, 69% recommend Canva and 86% approve of its CEO. This is self-selected feedback, not a representative employee survey; a numerical time-series trend was not verified.

Displayed 2025–2026 Glassdoor reviews mix praise for coworkers, benefits and learning with complaints about favoritism, bureaucracy and inconsistent leadership. These are anonymous employee opinions, not established misconduct.

Canva acknowledged that planned Teams pricing changes felt too sudden to some early adopters and retained their original pricing; it promised advance notice for future changes. Company response dated 2024-10-10 demonstrates historical pricing sensitivity, not a current churn estimate.

missing_fields: Audited consolidated financial statements, cash balance, cash flow, debt, net income and margins; latest filings were identified but underlying accounts were not obtained.
Revenue/ARR reconciliation, net retention, churn, customer concentration, cohort economics and AI gross margins.
Full funding history, exact primary capital raised, current cap table, preference terms, secondary transaction proceeds, buyers and final closing documentation.
Complete current executive roster and prior-company histories; CTO succession and exact final departure dates were not established from opened page text.
Current absolute headcount, comparable historical headcount series, current hiring pace and verified layoff history.
US music-litigation pleadings and current docket status; subsequent India patent proceedings after the opened judgment.
Comprehensive sanctions screening and regulatory/litigation clearance; no absence of exposure is asserted.
Quantified employee-review trend and independently measured current customer complaint/churn pattern.
Current 2026 realized financial results and a post-August-2025 priced financing valuation.

financial_signals.claim: Company claim: the 2025 year-in-review reported US$3.5 billion in revenue for 2025. The page is not an audited financial statement; do not equate this figure with exit annual recurring revenue.

Company claim via COO Cliff Obrecht: end-2025 ARR reached US$4 billion; B2B customers with more than 25 seats contributed US$500 million ARR, up 100%. ARR is a run-rate metric, not recognized annual revenue.
Company claim as of 2025-11-04: Canva remained profitable and had US$3.5 billion annualized revenue. The announcement does not quantify audited net income or margins.

Company claim in its 2025 CNBC Disruptor announcement: the global team expanded nearly 40%. The opened page does not specify the comparison period or absolute headcount; a precise current headcount trend remains unverified.

Forbes Australia reported on 2026-09-18, citing AFR, that Canva told investors in July 2026 to expect 20% revenue growth for 2026 rather than an earlier 30%, alongside product-rollout delays linked to rising AI costs. These are reported forecasts, not realized results.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: ASIC says Canva Pty Ltd, Canva Operations Pty Limited, Canva Trading Pty Ltd and Fusion Books Pty Ltd each paid A$198,000, totaling A$792,000, for alleged failure to lodge FY2024 reports by 2025-04-30. The consolidated report was lodged on 2026-03-27. Payment is not an admission or conviction. As of 2026-05-06.

ASIC states the Australian group restructured after 2024 and Canva Australia Holdings Pty Ltd lodged its FY2025 reports on 2026-04-30. This subsequent timely filing qualifies, but does not erase, the prior compliance issue.

Delhi High Court dismissed Canva’s appeal on 2026-01-28 against an interim patent injunction restricting its Present and Record feature in India. The court upheld INR50 lakh security for past use; findings remain prima facie, with merits for trial, not a final damages award.

Capital Brief reported competing Los Angeles Superior Court lawsuits between Canva and music-rights contractor Crunch Digital in September 2026: Canva alleged confidential-data disclosure; Crunch alleged breach/non-payment. These are reported allegations, not findings; underlying US pleadings and current docket status were not verified.

Canva’s incident FAQ says attackers accessed profile data for up to 139 million users on 2019-05-24. Its January 2020 update says approximately four million affected account passwords had been decrypted and that unchanged passwords were reset on 2020-01-12. Historical company disclosure, not a new 2026 breach.

UpGuard reported on 2025-06-09 that a My Jedai AI-chatbot database exposed survey responses linked to 571 unique Canva Creator email addresses. UpGuard notified the database owner on 2025-05-01 and confirmed remediation following its response the next day. This is third-party exposure, not proof of a direct Canva-system breach or a sanctioned-counterparty relationship.
